body.heading: More than dinner
paragraphs: A shared meal feeds people once. Cooking it together feeds them twice: once with food, and once with the particular closeness that only happens when hands are busy and nobody is performing.

Kids who cook tend to eat more adventurously. Teenagers who cook often talk more, because chopping onions is a famously good place to confess things. Adults who cook together remember they are a team.

body.heading: How to start small
paragraphs: Pick one meal a week — or a month — with a job for every person: washing, chopping, stirring, the playlist, setting the table like it matters. Jobs should be real; fake jobs fool no one over the age of six.
Let the food be imperfect and the kitchen be loud. The meal you remember in ten years will not be the flawless one; it will be the one with the smoke alarm and the story.

description: Cooking one meal together — messily, with real jobs for everyone — feeds a family twice.
